terms.gloss: it suits, it is convenient (for someone)
terms.grammar: phrase: neuter of commodus with esse, the person in the dative
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.48.2: id sī tibi erit commodum, cūrēs velim (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 1.2.38: dum erit commodum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “it pleases, is agreeable, = libet”. The adjective commodus is “suitable, convenient”, and of a person “obliging”; the noun commodum is an advantage.

terms.grammar: phrase: ex with the ablative; ex commodō tuō
evidence: Sen. Ep. 46.1: tamquam lēctūrus ex commodō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives it the opposite of festīnanter (Col. 6.2.14).

phrases.latin: id sī tibi erit commodum, cūrēs velim
phrases.english: if it suits you, I’d like you to see to it

phrases.latin: Crās veniam, sī tibi commodum est.
phrases.english: I’ll come tomorrow, if that suits you.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
